notes: KVM-style HDMI-over-Cat5e/6/6A extender sold as a TX/RX pair (IOGEAR calls them "CPU" side and "Console" side). CPU/transmitter unit: 1x HDMI in, 1x USB-B (uplink to host USB), 1x RJ45, 1x DC power in. Console/receiver unit: 1x HDMI out, 2x USB-A (keyboard + mouse), 1x RJ45, 1x DC power in, plus a 3.5mm analog audio de-embed output. Both TX and RX units are physically identical small metal enclosures (0.87 x 2.7 x 3.5 in) and both require their own 12V/1A DC power connection (with PoC/Power-over-Cable letting either end back-feed the other over the RJ45 run). Modeled here as a single device with all ports merged (TX-side and RX-side ports distinguished in the port names). Manufacturer spec table does not state an Ethernet speed grade for the RJ45 link (it's a proprietary HDBaseT-like signaling link over Cat5e/6/6A, not a standard switched-Ethernet port), so no eth-x.x grade was set. HDMI grade set to hdmi-2.0 based on stated 18Gbps/4K60 4:4:4 bandwidth (matches HDMI 2.0 spec, not HDMI 2.1). Several third-party retailer listing titles (e.g. CompSource, NetworkHardwares) state "2x HDMI Out / 4x USB", which appears to be an error/confusion with a different bundle SKU — the manufacturer's own spec table (iogear.com/products/gceh4k), cross-checked twice, and independently corroborated by B&H's search summary and Micro Center's summary, consistently show 1 HDMI in (CPU) + 1 HDMI out (Console) and USB-B (CPU) + 2x USB-A (Console). Direct HTML fetch of B&H/Amazon/Insight pages was blocked by anti-bot 403s; relied on WebFetch tool's rendered extraction plus manufacturer page as primary source.
